sources.citation: WALS Online, language 'Yi (Wuding-Luquan)' (yiw), all datapoints coded from Gao 1958.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress features (14A-17A) coded; only word-order chapters from Gao 1958.

sources.citation: Gao, Katie B. 2017. Dynamics of language contact in China: ethnolinguistic diversity and variation in Yunnan. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic survey of Wuding County (sec. 2.4.2.1 Nasu/Naisu/Aluo), phonology only for Miqie/Geipo; 'stress' appears only in non-linguistic senses.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) languages: a study from the perspectives of shared innovation and phylogenetic estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. 399 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Nothing. Nasu (Luquan/Wuding) sketch p.77: 46 initials, 20 vowels, 4 tones /55 33 2 11/ (after TBL 1992:666); toneme table 4.18 p.106. The words 'stress' and 'accent' occur nowhere in the dissertation.

sources.citation: Namkung, Ju (ed.). 1996. Phonological inventories of Tibeto-Burman languages (STEDT Monograph 3). Berkeley. Entries NASU pp.275-277 (after Chen Kang 1986; after Gao Huanian 1958 pp.4-14, Hetaojing village near Kunming, 7 tones) and LUQUAN p.231 (after Ma 1948 via Matisoff 1979).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; consonant/vowel/tone inventories only (Nasu tones 55 33 21 per Chen 1986; 55 44 33 32 24 213 21 per Gao 1958).

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Nasu language'; Wikipedia (zh) '彝語東部方言' (phonology after Huang Bufan ed. 1992 藏缅语族语言词汇).
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
sources.note: Nothing; 46 initials, 20 monophthong finals, 4 level tones 55/33/2/11.

sources.citation: Ma Xueliang 1948, 倮文作祭獻藥供牲經譯註, BIHP 20: 577 ff. — complete PDF
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only pp. 577-588 could be recovered (phonology section pp. 578-579 read in full and silent on stress); the complete open PDF should be re-downloaded from IHP when the host is reachable, for the record.

sources.citation: Ma Xueliang [馬學良]. 1948. 倮文作祭獻藥供牲經譯註. Bulletin of the Institute of History and Philology (史語所集刊) 20: 577 ff. (Luquan Lolo = Nasu, An-duo-kang village, priest Zhang Wenyuan's speech).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 二 標音說明 (pp.578-579) gives initials, plain vs laryngealised (緊喉) finals, four tones 55/33/11/2 (short tone glottal-checked) and tone-sandhi notes; no remark on stress or 輕重音.
